newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end modestly up, absorb profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end modestly up, absorb profit-taking.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed up 0.6 percent in another session of heavy trade, absorbing early profit-taking after Tuesday's strong rise, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares rose 465 points to close at 76,676 points.
Market volume was high at 661.9 million reais ($634.9 million) as foreign investors continued pumping fresh money into the market, traders said.
"Today's behavior shows the market's uptrend is consolidating and foreigners remain interested in our stocks," said a senior trader.

Wednesday's approval by a lower house committee of a constitutional amendment allowing presidential re-election was also seen as positive by market analysts, although it remains unclear when the bill will go for a vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate.

Analysts are confident the re-election bill will pass Congress, with a national plebiscite being the government's last resort to have the bill approved. Now the government's chances for a victory on the floor of the Chamber depend on its ability to persuade the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), Congress' largest, which is split on the issue.

Among top blue-chips, Telebras closed up 0.46 percent at 87.90 reais, while its common stock ended at 81.10 reais, up 0.26 percent. State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce continued climbing and rose 2.17 percent to close at 23.50 reais despite confusion over reports of a new gold and copper discovery in northern Brazil.
Traders said players remained speculating on the stock, noting that the company's share price was far behind other top blue-chips.
State oil firm Petrobras also posted further gains, closing at 188 reais, up 0.27 percent.
